ForgeMCP 0.2.17 — Stage 2E TedsOutliner Workaround Review

Checked October 24, 2026. Final verdict: BLOCKED — no safe project-local plugin workaround established. This was offline investigation only. No new isolated copy or launch plan was created because the required Phase 2 dependency gate failed. No Editor or commandlet was launched; production, installed Engine, ForgeMCP binaries/source, controller, historical test copies, and launch plans were not changed. The previous launch authorization remains consumed.

Ownership and assertion evidence

TedsOutliner is an Editor module of the installed experimental Engine plugin EditorDataStorageFeatures, not a standalone plugin. Its descriptor is [local path]. The failed child log mounted that plugin at line 67. CrashContext.runtime-xml records an assertion at ModuleManager.h:338 while requesting an unloaded LevelEditor module; its portable stack has UnrealEditor-TedsOutliner immediately below Core. Installed source .../Source/TedsOutliner/Private/TedsOutlinerModule.cpp lines 104–109 starts tab registration; lines 194–196 call GetModuleChecked<FLevelEditorModule>("LevelEditor"). This is a probable startup trigger. The stack is unsymbolized at function level, so that exact call is not conclusively proven. A matching UnrealEditor-TedsOutliner.pdb exists, but no installed symbolizer command was found in this offline pass; the minidump and PDB were left untouched.

The assertion preceded authenticated target-map and Landscape loading. Private DDC selection passed in the prior run. Stage 2E independent disk-backed height persistence remains untested.

Why disabling the plugin fails the required safety gate

[local path] sets DisableEnginePluginsByDefault=true and explicitly enables Fab. The installed Engine/Plugins/Fab/Fab.uplugin sets EditorDataStorageFeatures to Enabled=true in its plugin dependencies. The failed log mounted Fab at line 55 and EditorDataStorageFeatures at line 67, consistent with that chain. Fab source includes data-storage feature code (Source/Fab/Private/Teds/FabMyFolderIntegration.cpp) and registers Fab data-storage tables. This is a concrete functional dependency, not merely a similarly named module.

An explicit clone-project Enabled=false override for EditorDataStorageFeatures would conflict with the enabled Fab plugin's declared dependency. Disabling Fab instead would violate the requirement to preserve required project plugins and the user's established Fab workflow. The installed EditorDataStorageFeatures.uplugin groups TedsOutliner with other Editor modules; no supported project-local per-module exclusion was identified in the project/plugin descriptors or inspected UnrealBuildTool module-descriptor fields. Editing an installed Engine descriptor to change just TedsOutliner is prohibited and would not be a project-local workaround. A configuration-only assertion fix has therefore not been verified.

This finding does not assert that Fab uses the TedsOutliner UI itself. It establishes that the proposed plugin-wide disablement cannot be certified to preserve Fab. It also does not establish that a hypothetical module-level override would work at runtime. ForgeMCP, Landscape, World Partition, and LevelEditor are not proven safe under the proposed disablement because the required full dependency-preservation condition fails first.

Controller safety review retained from the prior diagnosis

The two WinError 31 entries for worker PIDs 38892 and 38252 occurred in the controller's retained-handle identity/liveness check path. The record does not prove either TerminateProcess call was attempted. The bounded observer identified workers by parent and then verified executable and creation identity through retained handles; the production PID was explicitly excluded. The isolated root was terminated by an identity-verified retained handle. Three other worker termination calls succeeded. The controller honestly marked shutdown verification incomplete because of the two exceptions, even though a later separate process query found the isolated root and all five recorded workers absent. No process was terminated during this review. A future controller diagnostic improvement could record the precise failing Win32 subcall and separate already-exited workers from identity-unverifiable workers without relaxing ownership checks; no controller edit is authorized here.

Preparation outcome and next boundary

No new clone, clone-only configuration change, source/clone manifest, private DDC, registration path, or proposed launch plan was prepared. As a result, no fresh source/clone hash comparison, disk-space gate, controller synthetic run, or runtime plugin-load verification is claimed for a future attempt. Historical evidence remains in the offline diagnosis and the failed Stage 2E execution report.

The next engineering decision is a separately scoped correction that preserves Fab: investigate a supported engine-side startup-order fix or a documented module-specific loading mechanism, and prove its dependency impact offline before preparing a new isolated copy. A future compiled fix would require build validation; an eventual independent runtime test would require a new explicit owner launch authorization. The existing approval cannot be reused. Stage 2E remains BLOCKED and Phase 6C is not approved.
